chunks: And from him, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ayyūb, who said:

I said to Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام: What is the minimum distance at which the traveler shortens? He said: A barīd. So there is no contradiction between these two reports and the first two reports, because the proper way to understand them is that when the traveler intends to return on the same day, shortening becomes obligatory for him over four farsakhs, and that which indicates this is:

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةِ فَرَاسِخَ: four farsakhs, a measured travel distance in legal rulings
key_terms.الْمُسَافِرُ: the traveler subject to legal rulings of journeying
key_terms.بَرِيدٌ: a barīd, a unit of travel distance

ai.seo_question: What is the minimum travel distance for shortening prayer according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the minimum travel distance requiring qasr prayer for a traveler. It explains that reports can be reconciled by understanding that if a traveler intends to return the same day, taqsir becomes obligatory over four farsakhs.
